discussion_comments.comment_body: we should never silence errors in tests.

Fixed: the prerender now collects the `onError` errors and the test asserts the abort reason (`This operation was aborted`). The assertion lands in the first commit and stays the same in the fix commit.

We can just abort with a string here and comment that we omit a stack because the stack isn't useful. The only useful part is the async stack ("which render completed?") which isn't available in this `error.stack`.

Done in `0f283ae` -- both changes as you described them.

The completion site now aborts with the string, and the comment gives your reason rather than mine:
the only stack worth having here is the async one that says which render completed, and that is not
in `error.stack`. The `stackTraceLimit` helper is gone with it, so nothing touches process-wide state
any more. I also removed the leak-framed comment on the `fatalError` path -- you are right that a
stack is the default and only its absence needs explaining.

Two things worth flagging rather than leaving for CI to find.

**An existing assertion had to change.** `ReactCache-test.js` on `main` asserts
`renderedCacheSignal.reason.message`, which is `undefined` once the reason is a string. It now
asserts the reason itself. That assertion predates this PR and is the only place in the suite that
depended on this reason being an `Error`.

**Why a string is safe on the consuming path**, since an earlier review here argued for keeping the
`Error` type: the reason reaches `erroredTask` through `abortStream`, `abortIterable` and
`abortBlob`, and from there `emitErrorChunk`, which already branches on `error instanceof Error` and
for a plain value produces `String(error)` with an empty stack. So this is a shape that path already
supports.

I also dropped the stack-invariant test this PR had added. With a string there is no stack to assert,
and your earlier point about it stands regardless.

The description is updated to match.

Updated the current PR.
Curious if this could swap actual errors we'd want to know about.

I don't think so tbh. once we've aborted we're claiming we don't have any interest in whatever is downstream. maybe the user hits the stop button and no more chunks will load and the stream will end up with connection closed error but if we intentionally aborted then this isn't salient information. I think it's similar to Fizz where a spawned task could error after an abort but we just don't care b/c it is as likely to have been caused by the conditions leading to the abort or the abort itself then anything actionable and independent
and actually if you had a lazily parsed model you would want to avoid a later error replacing the abort reason so this is probably quite important to the model being coherent
We should never throw conditionally on `__DEV__`. If so, it should be `console.error` instead.
done
This calls user code. Does it need to be wrapped in error handling? Didn't see where else that might be happening.

I think these are similar to `onRecoverableError`. I don't think they're handled properly in the existing one in `flushSpawnedWork` is right neither.

The way these phases flush is that they keep mutable state so that they can pick up and flush remaining phases if one is missed. So if this errors, then it errors the view transition which then flushes the remaining work which flushes the previous work but it doesn't flush this again so it probably misses anything after this. That means that bugs in React code might not be properly handled.

However, to ensure that other callbacks are handled, these should probably be wrapped in try/catch for each callback so that they're independently handled. Same thing for `onRecoverableError`.

There's also a question of what the default priority and execution context should be for these.

Question - would we expect / handle any of these instruction functions to throw here? I noticed a try-catch in `completeContainer`, but couldn't find what might throw in that function. Other instruction functions don't look like they would throw either

We should add a try-catch here if other functions can potentially throw (and React is expected to keep rendering). Inline scripts isolate failures, but the external runtime may skip processing further instructions / MutationRecords if one errors.
I think I ended up removing the throw but not the wrapping try catch. Good call on handling it here though, we probably should not actually throw and just return from completeContainer

We also log errors in the user console for other backend failures so that's not a concern.
Thank you. Honestly, I still have concerns about logging this to the user's page console, but I respect your opinion and will add the error-logging.
